# Jeremiah 34 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** While King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon was attacking Jerusalem with all his armies and the armies of every nation under his control, the LORD gave this message to Jeremiah:

**2** The LORD continued to speak about broken covenant with slaves through Jeremiah during that time.

**3** The LORD continued to speak about broken covenant with slaves through Jeremiah during that time.

**8** The LORD spoke to Jeremiah after King Zedekiah made a covenant with the people of Jerusalem to free all their slaves.

**17** "So the LORD says: You refused to obey Me by setting your countrymen free. Very well — I will set you 'free': free to be destroyed by war, disease, and famine! I will make you an object of horror to every nation on earth."

**18** The LORD continued to speak about broken covenant with slaves through Jeremiah during that time.

**19** The LORD continued to speak about broken covenant with slaves through Jeremiah during that time.

**22** The LORD continued to speak about broken covenant with slaves through Jeremiah during that time.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **34:1**: Jeremiah addresses broken covenant with slaves — a message that resonated far beyond its original audience.

- **34:11**: The freed then re-enslaved image powerfully captures the reality of faith under pressure.

- **34:22**: God's final word on this matter — spoken through fire and mud, exile and hope.

— PNEUMA
